title: Sony WH-1000XM4C launch for $299 alongside two more affordable headphones
snippet: As rumored, Sony is reviving its WH-1000XM4 headphones with a new WH-1000XM4C reboot, bringing some new colors to a much more affordable entry to the market compared to the company’s flagship. more…
fullText:
As rumored, Sony is reviving its WH-1000XM4 headphones with a new WH-1000XM4C reboot, bringing some new colors to a much more affordable entry to the market compared to the company’s flagship.

Sony’s flagship headphones are very good, but they’re also pricey. The current WH-1000XM6 retails for $460, though you can often save when buying on deals. But, now, Sony has a more affordable entry in this lineup with the new WH-1000XM4C.

This is a reboot of Sony’s 2020 flagship, which was equipped with USB-C and all of the sound and ANC you’d expect from a high-end pair of over-ear headphones. 

What’s new? Not a whole lot. Sony says to expect the same overall ANC and audio performance, but with the “latest sound tuning.” The hardware is mostly identical, though with new colors including Lavender, Black, and Platinum Silver.

	

They’re available for $299, well below Sony’s current flagship and in line with competitors such as Nothing Headphone (1). It’s borderline impossible to get a brand new pair of WH-1000XM4 nowadays, and even on the used market, you’re still spending around $250 or so in some cases. You might be able to find WH-1000XM5 for less – Amazon has frequent sales – but it’s likely these will see discounts in time too.

Beyond this, Sony is also introducing WH-CH730N and WH-CH530N as even more affordable over-ear headphones. At $179 and $69, they won’t deliver quite the same sound or ANC, but the value is there for certain. 

All three pairs support Fast Pair on Android. WH-1000XM4C will be later this month, with current shipping estimates on pre-orders landing around September 30, while the other two are launching this month.

title: Snap adds social event planning feature with Snapchat Plans
snippet: Snap is launching a new mobile app feature called Snapchat Plans. While it may sound like a new subscription service, Plans is actually a set of features that encourages hanging out in person. more…
fullText:
Snap is launching a new mobile app feature called Snapchat Plans. While it may sound like a new subscription service, Plans is actually a set of features that encourages hanging out in person.

Snap wants Snapchat users to meet up and hang out

“IRL meet-ups often start from a simple spark of conversation: A message turns into an idea, an idea turns into a plan, and time spent together becomes a memory,” Snap says.

“That’s why today we are introducing Snapchat Plans, a new suite of features that gives Snapchatters a new way to create, share, and manage their real-world plans with friends, all in one place.”

Snap highlights three current features, and one more coming soon, around Snapchat Plans: 

Send and receive invitations from mutual friends 

Track key details like time, date, and attendees 

Keep plans in one easy-to-find place

And soon, Snapchatters will be able to create events directly within a chat

The company explains how creating Snapchat Plans works in the app:

Snapchatters can add a title, choose a date and time, invite up to 200 friends, and personalize their event with dynamic Bitmoji-powered cover art that automatically updates as the plan comes together. Invitations are then delivered directly within a one-on-one chat with each invited friend, where guests can quickly RSVP with Going, Maybe, or Can’t Go without interrupting the conversation.

Here’s how it looks:

Importantly, Snap says that Snapchat Plans are both private and invite-only, so everything stays between friends. You can learn much more from Snap’s announcement post here.

Earlier this summer, Snap added a new Now Playing map feature to Snapchat.

Not a Snapchat user? Apple has its digital event planning service called Invites.
